title: Pork and Apple Casserole
subtitle: Sweet and savoury autumn braise
excerpt: Pork shoulder braised with apples, onion, cider, and a little cream. The apples soften into the sauce and balance the richness of the pork. Serve with roast potatoes or buttered noodles.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pork and apple is one of the most established flavour pairings in British and Northern European cooking. Braised versions with cider are common in the apple-growing regions of England and Normandy.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy lidded pot for braising.

content.text: Pork and apple casserole is a braise of diced pork shoulder with cooking apples, dry cider, and a finish of double cream. The apples break down gently into the sauce, giving it a sweet-savoury quality that cuts the richness of the pork. The whole thing needs about 90 minutes in the oven and looks after itself.

items.preparation: peeled, cored, and cut into wedges

content.text: Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Toss the pork with the flour, salt, and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large dutch oven over a high heat. Brown the pork in batches, about 3 minutes per batch, until golden. Lift out and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the apple wedges and cook for another 2 minutes, turning to lightly colour them.

Pour in the cider and stock. Scrape the base of the pot. Add the thyme and bay leaves. Return the pork and any resting juices. Bring to a simmer, cover, and transfer to the oven for 1 hour 30 minutes.

Once the pork is tender, lift it out and set aside. Remove the thyme and bay leaves. Stir the cream and mustard into the sauce. Place the pot back on the hob and simmer for 5 minutes to reduce slightly. Return the pork to the pot, taste for seasoning, and serve.
